body.title: Functional Classification and Planning Areas - Sidebar App

values.title: MRCOG Planning Areas and Roadway Functional Classification
values.splashContent:
How to use this web map application:

Use question mark button in the upper left of the map to view this information at any time.

Click on any feature on the map to see a pop-up box with more details. If your click identifies multiple features, arrows in the bottom left of the pop-up will let you browse through multiple pop-ups. The lower right of the pop-up will show more details about how many features you clicked.

On the left sidebar:

  • Legend shows what symbols on the map mean.
  • Basemap Gallery allows you to change the background map.
  • Details shows additional information about these layers.
  • Layers allows you to control the layers in the map:
    • Use the six dot icon to the left of each layer name to move layers up and down.
    • Use the check boxes to the left of each layer name to turn layers on or off. 
    • Use the shapes & lines icon to the far right of each layer name to view a mini-legend for that layer.
values.detailsContent:
AMPA

The Albuquerque Metropolitan Planning Area (AMPA) is MRMPO's planning area.

This area was revised in 2012-2013, with approval for revising by the Metropolitan Planning Board (MTB) on September 21, 2012, and the Governor of New Mexico on February 27, 2013.

The area was maintained in 2023, with approval for maintaining by the MTB on August 18, 2023, and by the New Mexico Department of Transportation (NMDOT) on February 1, 2024.

MRCOG & MRRTPO

The Mid-Region Council of Governments (MRCOG) region includes the AMPA (described above) and the Mid-Region Regional Transportation Planning Organization (MRRTPO). Local Planning Assistance (LPA) is offered throughout the MRCOG region by the Regional Planning Program (RPP).

Tribal Areas

This map uses Land Area Representations (LAR) from the Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA) to represent tribal areas. The To'Hajiilee Navajo Nation Chapter is also represented by BIA data. The Ojo Encino Navajo Nation Chapter and the 19 Pueblos District were manually digitized. 

Roadway Functional Classification

The Functional Classification system was updated in 2025. The system was approved by the MTB on October 17, 2025, and by the Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) on April 1, 2026.

Only select Local roads are shown. Any road not shown should be considered a Local road.

Adjusted Urban Areas

The Albuquerque and Los Lunas Adjusted Urban Areas include all roadways classified as "urban." Roadways outside of these areas are "rural." These areas were approved by the MTB on August 18, 2023, and by NMDOT on February 1, 2024.

Road Owners

Road ownership is modeled and should not be considered authoritative. It is based on data from state and local agencies. Please contact us to correct any mistakes (gis@mrcog-nm.gov).

Other Areas

NMDOT District Boundaries are provided by NMDOT. 

County boundaries are provided by the US Census Bureau.

Incorporated Places (i.e., municipalities) are provided by the municipalities themselves and/or the New Mexico Taxation & Revenue Department (NMTRD).

expressionInfos.title: Total Area (Square Miles)
expressionInfos.expression:
//expression to convert from square meters to square miles.

var l = $feature.AREALAND
var w = $feature.AREAWATER
var a = (l / 1000) * 0.000386
var b = (w / 1000) * 0.000386

body.title: Sidebar
body.description:
Sidebar includes a set of tools and options that appear alongside of the map that allow viewers to interact with and update data. Enable editing tools to allow app viewers to add and update features in the map. Configure filters that app viewers can use to gain more information about your data. Include bookmarks to guide your viewers to important regions and add essential map tools viewers can use to explore the map. 

Examples:
  • Present a detailed map of population data with supplementary text for further explanation
  • Allow data reviewers to investigate and update records as needed with editing tools
  • Create an app that presents public services with the ability for viewers to filter for the types of services they need

Data Requirements
This application has no data requirements.

Key App Capabilities
  • Cover page - Include a cover page to introduce viewers to your app
  • Edit tools - Provide the option to add and update features, includes support for snapping
  • Filter options - Configure predefined options that allow viewers to filter data in the map
  • Bookmarks - Zooms and pans the map to a collection of preset extents that are saved in the scene
  • Export - Capture an image of the map to export
  • Measurement tools - Provide tools to measure distance and area
  • Basemap gallery - Display a collection of basemaps that offers the ability choose and replace the current basemap in a map
  • Language switcher - Publish a multilingual app that combines your translated custom text and the UI translations for supported languages
  • Home, Zoom Controls, Legend, Layer List, Search

Supportability
This web app is designed responsively to be used in browsers on desktops, mobile phones, and tablets. We are committed to ongoing efforts towards making our apps as accessible as possible. Please feel free to leave a comment on how we can improve the accessibility of our apps for those who use assistive technologies.
body.snippet: Display a map alongside tools that edit, filter, and interact with data
